update.title: Built a timeline-based portfolio site
update.summary: Built a framework-free portfolio that loads project metadata from one JSON file, highlights featured work, and expands timeline entries as they move through the viewport.

preview.description: Dark portfolio project timeline with one centered project entry expanded between compact neighboring entries

blocks.body:
## Make the timeline the primary way through the work

The homepage gives one project a larger introduction, then organizes the work as a chronological timeline. The entry nearest the center of the viewport expands with a larger preview, fuller summary, tags, and a direct project link. Keyboard focus triggers the same treatment.

Nearby entries remain compact, keeping the chronology visible as the reader moves through the page.

blocks.description: Dark portfolio project timeline with one centered project entry expanded between compact neighboring entries. The focused timeline entry expands while the surrounding work remains visible in sequence.

blocks.body:
## Keep publishing simple

Project metadata now lives in `projects/projects.json`. The homepage fetches that file, selects the featured project, sorts the records by date, and renders the timeline.

Each project keeps its own detail page and assets under `projects/<slug>/`. The complete site remains plain HTML, CSS, JavaScript, JSON, and project assets, ready to deploy directly to static hosting without an application server or build step.

blocks.code:
flowchart LR
  JSON[projects.json] --> Featured[Featured project]
  JSON --> Sort[Sort projects by date]
  Sort --> Timeline[Interactive timeline]
  Assets[Project previews] --> Featured
  Assets --> Timeline
  Timeline --> Pages[Project detail pages]
blocks.description: One metadata file supplies both the featured project and the chronological timeline, while each project retains an independent static page.
